newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela says France would veto Salim for U.N..
newsitem.headline: Mandela says France would veto Salim for U.N..

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Sunday French President Jaques Chirac would veto Tanzania's Salim Ahmed Salim as U.N. secretary-general because he was not fluent in French.

Mandela told a news conference South Africa had nominated the Tanzanian, who is now secretary-general of the Organisation of African Unity, partly because of his support for the anti- apartheid struggle.
"But we are having opposition to him," he said.

"I spoke at length last night to Jacques Chirac, who insists that a candidate for the secretary-generalship of the United Nations must be fluent in both English and French, and he is not prepared to support any candidate who does not have these qualifications," Mandela told a news conference.
"He said he will veto Salim Salim if he is nominated," Mandela said, describing Salim as "a highly capable man".
"He has done very well as secretary-general of the OAU... We think he is the best candidate for the job."

The OAU, which threw its weight behind Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali at its annual summit in Cameroon in July, opened the door to other Africans when the Egyptian set aside his candidacy last Wednesday after a November 19 U.S. veto in the Security Council blocked his path to the now traditional second term.
Mandela said he had tried in vain to persuade his U.S. counterpart Bill Clinton to drop his opposition to Boutros- Gali.
"We have spoken to Clinton several times on this question but we have not been able to sway them not to veto (Boutros- Ghali)," he said.
Salim was in the West African state of Togo on Sunday for talks with veteran Francophone President Gnassingbe Eyadema.
"What is certain is that Africa has the right to a second term as U.N. secretary-general," Salim told Togo's state television, saying some African leaders had asked him to stand.
